quests.textToSpeak: Leave it to cool before you take the lid off.
quests.textWithBlanks: Leave it to ___ before you take the lid off.
quests.explanation: Leave it to cool, to set and to soak are three real kitchen instructions with three different results. Leave it to is spoken as one quick block, so the verb arrives without warning.
quests.hint: To become less hot.

quests.textToSpeak: Make sure you stir it every couple of minutes.
quests.textWithBlanks: Make sure you ___ it every couple of minutes.
quests.explanation: Stir, turn and shake are all things you do to food at intervals, and each is one short syllable. Make sure you signals that this step really matters.
quests.hint: To move it around with a spoon so it does not stick.

quests.textToSpeak: Whatever you do, don't skip that step.
quests.textWithBlanks: Whatever you do, don't ___ that step.
quests.explanation: Don't skip it, don't rush it and don't repeat it are three separate warnings about the same step. Whatever you do at the start tells you a strong instruction is coming.
quests.hint: To leave it out completely and move on.

quests.textToSpeak: To be fair, she did warn us about the cost.
quests.textWithBlanks: To be fair, she did ___ us about the cost.
quests.explanation: Warn us, tell us and remind us are all possible, but warn implies she predicted trouble. To be fair signals the speaker is admitting a point against their own side.
quests.hint: To tell someone in advance that there is a risk.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I see what you mean, but I'm not entirely convinced.
quests.textWithBlanks: I see what you mean, but I'm not entirely ___.
quests.explanation: Not entirely convinced, sure or certain are three polite ways of disagreeing, and all three are equally natural here. English speakers soften disagreement with not entirely rather than saying no.
quests.hint: Persuaded that something is true.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I'm with you on the price, but not on the timing.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'm with you on the price, but not on the ___.
quests.explanation: The pattern I'm with you on X but not on Y separates agreement from disagreement, and any topic can fill either slot. Timing, location and design are all things a team argues about.
quests.hint: When something is scheduled to happen.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Our connection was really tight, so we nearly missed the second flight.
quests.textWithBlanks: Our ___ was really tight, so we nearly missed the second flight.
quests.explanation: A tight connection, schedule or transfer would all explain nearly missing a flight. Connection is the standard travel word for changing from one service to another.
quests.hint: The link between one flight and the next.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: They put us up in a hotel overnight at their expense.
quests.textWithBlanks: They put us up in a hotel overnight at their ___.
quests.explanation: At their expense means they paid, at their cost means roughly the same, but at their request means they only asked for it. One noun decides who is out of pocket.
quests.hint: Money that someone else pays out.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The insurance covered most of it, thankfully.
quests.textWithBlanks: The insurance ___ most of it, thankfully.
quests.explanation: Covered, refunded and paid are all things insurance can do, with slightly different timing. Covered means the policy took responsibility from the start.
quests.hint: Included in the policy, so you did not have to pay.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I'm hoping to negotiate a slightly higher salary.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'm hoping to ___ a slightly higher salary.
quests.explanation: Negotiate, request and justify a salary are three different approaches to the same conversation. Negotiate assumes there is room to move on both sides.
quests.hint: To discuss terms until both sides agree.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The rent's due on the first of every month.
quests.textWithBlanks: The rent's ___ on the first of every month.
quests.explanation: Rent that's due has not been paid yet, while rent that's paid or collected already has. One word tells you whether you still owe money.
quests.hint: It has to be handed over by then.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: It works out cheaper if you pay annually.
quests.textWithBlanks: It works out cheaper if you pay ___.
quests.explanation: Works out cheaper means the total ends up lower, and paying annually, monthly or upfront are the usual options. Annually and monthly share the same ending, so listen to the front.
quests.hint: Once a year, in a single payment.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I've been getting into the habit of walking after dinner.
quests.textWithBlanks: I've been getting into the habit of ___ after dinner.
quests.explanation: Getting into the habit of walking, reading or stretching after dinner are all believable new routines. The blank follows a long run of unstressed words, which is exactly where listeners drift.
quests.hint: Going out on foot, gently, for exercise.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: She's given up caffeine completely.
quests.textWithBlanks: She's given up caffeine ___.
quests.explanation: Given up completely, temporarily and recently tell three different stories about the same decision. Adverbs at the end of a sentence are often rushed, so they are easy to lose.
quests.hint: Totally, with nothing left at all.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Getting eight hours' sleep makes a huge difference.
quests.textWithBlanks: Getting eight hours' sleep makes a huge ___.
quests.explanation: Makes a huge difference, impact and improvement are all natural, though difference is by far the most common in speech. The phrase make a difference is worth learning as one unit.
quests.hint: A noticeable change for the better.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Have you tried switching it off and on again?
quests.textWithBlanks: Have you tried ___ it off and on again?
quests.explanation: Switching it off and on, turning it off and on, and plugging it back in are the three things every helpdesk suggests first. Switching and turning are interchangeable here, so only sound separates them.
quests.hint: Using the power button.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The app keeps logging me out for no reason.
quests.textWithBlanks: The app keeps ___ me out for no reason.
quests.explanation: Logging me out, signing me out and kicking me out all describe the same annoying thing, with kicking being the most informal. The -ing verb sits between keeps and me, where speech runs fastest.
quests.hint: Ending your session so you have to enter your details again.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: It might be worth backing everything up first.
quests.textWithBlanks: It might be worth backing everything up ___.
quests.explanation: Backing everything up first, anyway or instead give three different pieces of advice about the same action. It might be worth is a gentle English way of making a strong recommendation.
quests.hint: Before anything else happens.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: How's it going with the house move?
quests.textWithBlanks: How's it going with the house ___?
quests.explanation: The house move, the house search and the house renovation are three separate stages, and any of them could be going on. How's it going with is the standard opener for asking about ongoing news.
quests.hint: Changing address and going to live somewhere else.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Not bad, thanks. Busy as ever.
quests.textWithBlanks: Not bad, thanks. ___ as ever.
quests.explanation: Busy as ever, tired as ever and same as ever are all standard replies to how are you. As ever means nothing has changed, which is the point of this kind of small talk.
quests.hint: Having far too much to do.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: It's been one of those weeks, to be honest.
quests.textWithBlanks: It's been one of those ___, to be honest.
quests.explanation: One of those weeks, days or mornings all mean it has been difficult, but they cover very different stretches of time. To be honest at the end softens the complaint.
quests.hint: Seven-day periods.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I'd have thought they'd have said something by now.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'd have thought they'd have ___ something by now.
quests.explanation: This sentence stacks two reduced forms, I'd've and they'd have, before the verb even arrives. Said, mentioned and noticed are all plausible, so you must stay with the sentence to the end.
quests.hint: Spoken some words about it.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: He must've forgotten about the whole thing.
quests.textWithBlanks: He ___ forgotten about the whole thing.
quests.explanation: Must've expresses near certainty, might've expresses possibility, and would've imagines something unreal. In speech all three collapse into a single fast syllable plus 'uv'.
quests.hint: The speaker is almost certain this is the explanation.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: There isn't much milk left, is there?
quests.textWithBlanks: There isn't ___ milk left, is there?
quests.explanation: There isn't much, any or enough milk left are all correct English with different shades of meaning. Much and any are weak, unstressed words that almost vanish between isn't and milk.
quests.hint: A quantity word used with uncountable things like milk.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The flat upstairs has been empty for months.
quests.textWithBlanks: The flat ___ has been empty for months.
quests.explanation: The flat upstairs, downstairs and next door are all neighbours, and any of them could be empty. These position words are compounds, stressed on the first part.
quests.hint: On the floor above yours.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: They're putting up scaffolding at the end of the street.
quests.textWithBlanks: They're putting up ___ at the end of the street.
quests.explanation: Putting up scaffolding, fencing and signs are all street works, and all three nouns follow put up naturally. Scaffolding is long but unstressed after the first syllable.
quests.hint: The metal frame builders climb on to work high up.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The landlord's finally agreed to fix the boiler.
quests.textWithBlanks: The landlord's finally agreed to fix the ___.
quests.explanation: A landlord could agree to fix the boiler, the roof or the lock, so the complaint could be about anything. Finally agreed suggests the tenant has been asking for a long time.
quests.hint: The unit that heats the water and the radiators.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: You might want to run that past Priya first.
quests.textWithBlanks: You might want to run that ___ Priya first.
quests.explanation: Run it past someone and run it by someone both mean check with them, while run it through means look at it in detail. You might want to is a soft way of giving an instruction at work.
quests.hint: Run something ___ someone means ask their opinion first.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: We could always push it to next quarter if needs be.
quests.textWithBlanks: We ___ always push it to next quarter if needs be.
quests.explanation: We could always suggests an option, we should always gives advice, and we might always is weaker still. If needs be is a fixed phrase meaning if it becomes necessary.
quests.hint: A modal suggesting a possible option, not advice or obligation.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I'd rather we didn't commit to anything just yet.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'd rather we didn't ___ to anything just yet.
quests.explanation: Commit to, agree to and respond to anything are all grammatical here, but commit is the strongest. I'd rather we didn't is a very English way of saying please don't.
quests.hint: To bind yourself to a decision you cannot easily undo.
